div.p: Simulation based studies are inevitable in the field of real time scheduling, due to the difficulty in remodeling the existing Real Time Operating System (RTOS) to incorporate new scheduling policies. This paper presents a real time simulator-ERTSim, which can be used for solving scheduling problems in the real time domain. The features of ERTSim includes: Graphical User Interface (GUI), synthetic task generation algorithms, modules for feasibility tests, implementation of task scheduling algorithms and generating execution traces for visual understanding. ERTSim is developed using structured C and C++ class functions.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: The field of real time scheduling is a well established, progressing and challenging domain within the fields of real time systems. There exist still a volume of issues yet to be solved in the field. The advancement and improvements in the technology had led to an era where; sophistication and compact portable device structure have become predominant. Application exhibiting real time nature has more complex and stringent time constraints to be met. Development and implementation of such systems are hard at the hardware level and a simulation based study becomes unavoidable under such cases. The aid of a simulator tool is beneficial to check and verify the existing issues in real time systems. One of the major topics in the field is scheduling of real time tasks on uni and multiprocessor systems. An optimal scheduling decision helps the real time application to deliver the correct functionality meeting all the temporal constraints. To test and compare different scheduling algorithms for performance evaluation becomes hard in the absence of a good simulation tool.

There are available only a few real time simulators which can be used for solving the problems existing the field of real time systems. Some of the existing simulators pertain to only a particular execution pattern and has limited features. Different simulators have different capacities and have their own limitations too. This paper proposes a real time simulator which can be used to solve the major issues existing in the real time field. Also, ERTSim can be used an effective teaching and learning tool to understand the basics of real time systems. The major contributions include: The rest of the paper is organized as: section 2 contains a brief detail about the related works done in the field followed by details regarding the ERTSim simulator in section 3. Section 4 describes results with examples to illustrate the use of ERTSim simulator. Finally, section 5 concludes the paper.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: The literature shows a support for few real time task simulators to learn the real time basics and to test and schedule real time jobs. Some of them include: RTSim, Chedder, Rapid-RMA and YASA. RTSim [1] is a popular real time simulator used for performance evaluation under varying load conditions. Chedder [2] is a freely accessible simulator which has an editor and framework to include scheduling policies and feasibility tests. Rapid-RMA [3] and YASA [4] also provides similar functionalities and features. In [5], a web based real time task scheduler was proposed which can be used an effective teaching tool to teach the real time basics. There are available similar frameworks within the field. Sergio et al. [6] provided a complete hardware based architecture that utilizes slack times and uses optimal algorithms to function effectively in the hardware. In [7], a tool for learning real time aspects is presented where the previous architecture could be stored and retrieved later for future comparison. YARTISS [8] is a scheduling simulator for scheduling real time tasks in a multi-processor system. The basic objective of the proposed simulator is to check and compare the user defined scheduling algorithms with that of the classical existing ones in the field. Matsubara et al. [9] proposed a scheduling simulator suitable for developing real time applications with application modeling capabilities. In [10], a framework for development of a MATLAB based real time simulator was proposed. The basic features supported include task scheduling, feasibility tests and performance evaluation module. The basic architecture of the proposed real time simulator is changed from MATLAB based simulator to a C/C++ based simulator in this work, to make it a more effective and open source tool for use.

div.head: III. ERTSim SIMULATOR FRAMEWORK AND FEATURES
div.p: ERTSim simulator is developed using individual C++ functions which communicates with the users through a GUI. A user friendly GUI which comprises of various buttons to add different functions, makes it easy for the users to handle different features of real time systems. The basic block diagram of ERTSim is shown in Fig. 1.

div.head: Fig. 1: Basic block diagram of ERTSim
div.p: The ERTSim simulator comprises of a collection of functions written in C/C++ language, which enables the users to execute the functions by providing appropriate inputs and observing the expected output. The front end of ERTSim is shown in Fig. 2.

div.head: Fig. 2: Front end of ERTSim
div.p: The different features incorporated in ERTSim include:

div.head: A. Task Generate
div.p: For testing and evaluating different algorithms, a varying workload is necessary as an input. In a way, the performance of different algorithms and protocols depends on the task input on which the algorithm is tested. Therefore, a uniform varying work load is important for such cases. ERTSim includes a Task Generate button, which is useful for generating work load with existing well known and proven algorithms like: UUnifast, UScaling and UFitting [11]. They are widely accepted task generation algorithms in the field. For this function, the number of tasks and the total task set utilization is to given as the user input.

div.head: B. Task Nature
div.p: Even though most of the real time tasks considered is of periodic nature, in practical cases, it is not always true. The real world tasks can be of aperiodic or sporadic in nature. The ERTSim simulator has provision to include tasks of:

Periodic tasks have regular intervals defined between successive instance occurrences. But, in the case of an aperiodic task, there is no periodicity of occurrence of instances. Aperiodic tasks are admitted to the system once they pass the acceptance test [12]. Acceptance tests are measures to find if there exist any slack times where in the aperiodic task instances can be run. Sporadic tasks are also aperiodic tasks but, there is an inter arrival time defined between the occurrence of successive instances.

div.head: C. Feasibility Tests
div.p: It is beneficial for most of the application development to test and verify the feasibility of the method to be applied before implementation. In the case of real time scheduling, before executing a proposed schedule, it is always desirable to check the feasibility of the schedule before run time. ERTSim is incorporated with and necessary condition for schedulability check for both fixed priority and dynamic priority systems are Response Time Analysis [13]. RTA works well with the assumption that deadline of each task instance is equal to the time period. In case, when task deadlines are either less than or equal to the time periods, then for EDF scheduling algorithms Processor Demand Analysis can be used for checking the schedulability of the task set.

div.head: D. Task Scheduling
div.p: Tasks are scheduled on a uniprocessor system based on different strategies. There are a variety of scheduling policies and algorithms available in the field which are very popular and classical ones. The broad range of classification of such algorithms is: fixed priority and dynamic priority assignment. The major scheduling algorithms existing in the field [14], as listed below are incorporated in ERTSim simulator.
• Rate Monotonic (RM) algorithm • Deadline Monotonic (DM) algorithm • Earliest Deadline First (EDF) algorithm

div.head: E. Execution Trace
div.p: For an easy understanding, the execution trace of each scheduling algorithms are plotted and displayed in ERTSim by the press of Trace button. This gives the user a better and clear visual understanding.

div.head: IV. RESULTS WITH EXAMPLE
div.p: To understand the functioning of ERTSim real time simulator, each functionality is explained with a simple example in this section. Task Generate module creates synthetic tasks, to be fed as an input for different scheduling algorithms. When the user click on the Task Generate button, the different algorithms for task generation are displayed and upon the selection of one of the algorithms, it asks for number of tasks and required processor utilization. The corresponding functionality is shown in Fig. 3, when UUnifast algorithm is used to generate a total number of 10 tasks with processor utilization of 0.96. The different task parameters generated by the algorithm can be seen in Fig. 3.

div.head: Fig. 3 Task Generate function of ERTSim
div.p: Similarly, any other task generation algorithm can be used in a similar way. In Fig. 4, the Feasibility Tests module functioning is shown.
